title: Contrast and visibility issues with default light theme options
body: ### Tested versions - Reproduced in: v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb] - I didn't test previous versions as I'm not using any at the moment besides 4.7.1 ### System information Godot v4.7.1.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.6.2) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M4 Max - Apple M4 Max (16 threads) - 48.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description Hello, for the selection of built-in light themes, there's contrast issues in some areas of the viewport and the toolbar above it, see some of these examples: 1. When I select the "Light" color preset, these viewport buttons (`zoom in`, `zoom out` and `center view`) are in a dark shade that makes it not very easy to see compared to the gray background: 2. In the toolbar, particularly when opening the `Anchor Preset` menu, the contrast is quite poor, making it impossible to distinguish the shapes of each option: One has to hover over it basically to see its shape (or have it selected beforehand also) Now, compare these to the default theme: These issues are shared by the `Solarized (Light)` theme: Thank you so much beforehand and I appreciate all good things Godot has contributed to the indie scene ### Steps to reproduce Go to **Editor Settings**, then search for the **Interface** section, select the **Theme** option. Look for **Color Preset**, then choose either the `Light` theme or `Solarized (Light)` theme, then exit the **Editor Settings** menu and see the zoom in/zoom out buttons for example, or add an UI node and open the anchor preset menu ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) I'm not sure I can share a project that also includes the editor settings, this is an issue with the themes not the engine itself
